about.title: About Volume Converter
about.description: The Volume Converter converts between different units of volume and capacity. From liters to gallons, milliliters to fluid ounces, this converter handles common volume measurements used in cooking, chemistry, engineering, and everyday life. Volume conversion is useful in cooking, scientific reference work, manufacturing, and international trade. Whether you're following recipes, measuring chemicals, calculating fuel consumption, or reviewing liquid specifications, this tool helps compare metric and imperial volume systems.

faq.q: What volume units does the converter support?
faq.a: Our volume converter supports metric units (liters, milliliters, cubic meters), imperial units (gallons, quarts, pints, fluid ounces), and cooking units (cups, tablespoons, teaspoons) across common volume-conversion needs.

faq.q: What's the difference between US and UK gallons?
faq.a: A US gallon equals 3.785 liters (231 cubic inches), while a UK imperial gallon equals 4.546 liters (277.42 cubic inches). Our converter clearly distinguishes between these two gallon types.

faq.q: How accurate are the volume conversions?
faq.a: All volume conversions use precise mathematical formulas with decimal accuracy. Our converter is suitable for scientific reference, cooking recipes, chemistry checks, and general comparison use.

faq.q: Can I convert cooking measurements accurately?
faq.a: Yes, our converter includes precise cooking units: 1 cup = 240 mL, 1 tablespoon = 15 mL, 1 teaspoon = 5 mL. Perfect for recipe conversions and international cooking.

faq.q: How do I convert liters to gallons?
faq.a: To convert liters to US gallons, divide by 3.785. For UK gallons, divide by 4.546. For example, 10 liters = 2.64 US gallons or 2.20 UK gallons. Our converter handles this automatically.

faq.q: What about dry vs liquid measurements?
faq.a: Our converter focuses on volume measurements for liquids and gases. For dry ingredients in cooking, weight conversions may be more accurate since density varies by ingredient type.
